headline: Mechanistic models link microbial colony and biofilm structure to physical drivers
label: Microbial Colony Physical Modeling
summary: Quantitative models now couple geometry, force balance, and resource limitation to discrete microbial outcomes such as separation and detachment.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit mechanistic attribution in microbial populations: each model ties a defined structural or spatial outcome to a specific physical or chemical driver. The Pseudomonas aeruginosa study combines quantitative density measurements with a minimal biophysical model and attributes sibling colony separation to nutrient depletion rather than lethal inhibition. The Staphylococcus epidermidis model applies force balance to biofilm cell cluster detachment, tracking size and shape under varying EPS adhesion disruption and benchmarking to 24-hour data. The microgravity simulation work is more methodological, improving a growth functional form to isolate gravity-driven flow and sedimentation, and does not report a discrete outcome of the same kind. What is new is coupling geometry and mechanical force balance, or resource limitation, to discrete outcomes such as separation and detachment.
